Attach an annual NIS companion to Core discharges

Source: R/open-companion.R
nis_join_companion.Rd

Attach an annual NIS companion to Core discharges

Usage

nis_join_companion(x, path, component, columns)

Arguments

x

A lazy Core query from nis_open(), including its linkage fields.

path

Directory containing Parquet for one companion component, using the annual or Hive layout accepted by nis_open(). Keep Core and each companion in separate directories, with parts from the same release.

component

One of "hospital", "severity", or "dx_pr_grps".

columns

Character vector of companion fields to add. Names are matched case-insensitively using DuckDB's identifier rules. Choose fields with names distinct from fields in x.

Value

A lazy DuckDB-backed Core query with the requested columns added.

Details

Hospital uses YEAR and HOSP_NIS. Severity and Diagnosis and Procedure Groups use YEAR and KEY_NIS. Include companion parts for every year opened in x. A field supplied only in some of those years is missing in the others. A discharge without a matching companion row is retained with missing companion values.

DuckDB checks for missing, duplicate, or incompatible companion keys before constructing the left join. Uniqueness in the Core key types guarantees exactly one output row per input discharge. Keep both sets of Parquet files in place until the lazy query is evaluated.

Use hospital characteristics to describe discharges and compare discharge outcomes. The joined rows and weights still represent discharges. The Hospital file's TOTAL_DISC counts sampled discharges and is excluded from this helper. HCUP's post-2011 design does not support estimating individual hospital volumes.

See also

Opening NIS data, HCUP NIS File Specifications.

Examples

path <- tempfile()
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp3Fj7Fz/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
write_component <- function(component, fields) {
  folder <- file.path(path, component)
  dir.create(folder, recursive = TRUE)
  file <- DBI::dbQuoteString(con, file.path(folder, "NIS_2020.parquet"))
  DBI::dbExecute(con, paste0("COPY (SELECT ", fields, ") TO ", file, " (FORMAT PARQUET)"))
}
write_component("core", "2020 AS YEAR, 1 AS KEY_NIS, 7 AS HOSP_NIS")
#> [1] 1
write_component("hospital", "7 AS HOSP_NIS, 2 AS HOSP_BEDSIZE")
#> [1] 1
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
nis_open(file.path(path, "core"), check_release = FALSE) |>
  nis_join_companion(file.path(path, "hospital"), "hospital", "HOSP_BEDSIZE") |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp3Fj7Fz/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   HOSP_NIS KEY_NIS  YEAR HOSP_BEDSIZE
#>      <int>   <int> <int>        <int>
#> 1        7       1  2020            2
